Documentation → Releases → 3.3.0

SATOM 3.3.0

Operations opens on a Wiki the team writes for itself, the HTTP Observatory reverts its own fixes and adds a Content Security Policy in Report-Only first, and device alerts say which reading crossed which limit.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Wiki
  • HTTP Observatory
  • Device alerts
  • Fixed
  • Before you upgrade
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-10-16 · All releases

In short#

Operations › Wiki is new: articles the people who run the console write for each other, published to Global or to chosen ADOMs and limited to profiles or groups when needed. The HTTP Observatory can now undo the fixes it applied, starts a Content Security Policy in Report-Only, and knows the HSTS preload list. Device alerts name the reading and the limit that fired.

What's new#

Wiki#

  • Wiki is the first entry of Operations in every device ADOM and of the Global block.
  • Who can read it: Global (ticked by default) or chosen ADOMs, and optionally some profiles or Wiki groups. An article you may not read does not exist for you — not listed, not counted, not found by its address.
  • Finding articles: a menu with New article, a search across title, description, text, tags, author and topics, the topic tree with counts, and the tags; filters by ADOM, status, topic, tag and Mine.
  • Writing: a rich-text editor that stores Markdown. Changes are saved automatically as a draft; readers keep the published version until someone presses Publish, which makes a new numbered version. History keeps every version.
  • Editing together: anyone with Write Wiki articles who can read an article can edit its text. If someone else saved first, your save is refused and nothing is overwritten. The audience, archiving and deleting stay with the author and the moderators.

See Wiki.

HTTP Observatory#

  • Revert a fix: every set of fixes applied from the page can be undone from History → Fixes applied. A value changed on the appliance since the fix is left as it is, and the page says so.
  • Content Security Policy in two steps: a site without a CSP first gets it in Report-Only, so nothing breaks while you watch the reports; the second step enforces the same policy.
  • HSTS preload list: a site on Chromium's preload list is graded as the MDN Observatory grades it. The list is refreshed daily.
  • Exports: Export CSV of the published sites and a PDF report per scan.
  • Nightly grading of every published site is scheduled by default.

See HTTP Observatory.

Device alerts#

An alert now reads Device {device} is critical — CPU 97.0% (critical 95%) instead of 1/6 probes alerting. The body lists each alerting probe with its reading, its limits and where each limit is set. See Alerting.

Fixed#

  • Alert mail inserted device text unescaped and ran multi-line findings into one paragraph; the in-app notification cut the detail at 400 characters (now 1,500).
  • The HTTP Observatory site picker labels added in 3.2.1 were untranslated in German, French, Italian and Spanish.
  • On a phone the ADOM chooser shown after sign-in could not be scrolled; it now scrolls, and on narrow screens each ADOM is a compact row.

Before you upgrade#

  • This release is published as source on GitHub (tag v3.3.0). No new installers, container image or offline update package were built for it; the newest of those remain the 3.1.0 ones.
  • Database change: the Wiki tables and the Observatory fix history are added by migrations applied on restart (satom execute restart-all runs them on the primary).
  • Custom profiles get the Wiki permissions only when an administrator adds them under Profiles; the readonly, operator and admin system profiles have them already.

Learn more#

  • Full list of changes: the CHANGELOG in the repository.
